meta.title: Ad Budget Calculator and Media Buying Plan
meta.description: Answer four questions, enter your numbers and get a monthly ad budget, expected results and a budget split for Meta and Google Search.

title: Build your media buying plan
intro: Answer four quick questions, then fill in the tabs. Everything stays in your browser.

businessType.title: What kind of business are you planning for?
businessType.hint: This decides which numbers we ask for and how we judge profit.

accountStatus.title: Does the ad account have previous data?
accountStatus.hint: With data we start from your real costs. Without it we plan a test first.

platforms.title: Which platforms will you use?
platforms.hint: Pick one or both. More platforms are on the way.

goalType.title: What is your goal?
goalType.hint: Tell us how many results you want, or how much you can spend.

leads.label: Lead generation
leads.desc: You collect leads, then book calls or appointments that turn into clients.

ecommerce.label: Ecommerce
ecommerce.desc: You sell products online and customers buy on your store.

new.label: New account
new.desc: No useful history yet. We will plan a test budget and decision rules.

existing.label: Has previous data
existing.desc: At least a few weeks of spend and results we can learn from.

target.label: Target number of results
target.desc: I know how many clients or sales I want each month.

budget.label: Fixed monthly budget
budget.desc: I know how much I can spend each month.

tabs.label: Planner sections
tabs.fixErrors: {count, plural, one {Fix # issue to calculate} other {Fix # issues to calculate}}

tabIntro.setup: Tell us what you sell, where and when. This sets benchmarks, seasonality and currency.
tabIntro.business: Your business numbers set the limits: what you can afford to pay for a lead, a client or a sale.
tabIntro.account: Enter the results from your ad accounts for a recent period, or import a CSV export.
tabIntro.estimates: Your best estimates for a new account. Pick a source for each one so we know how confident to be.
tabIntro.planning: How you plan to structure campaigns and creative testing.
tabIntro.advanced: Sensible defaults are already filled in. Change them only if you know your accounts behave differently.

niche.label: Niche
niche.tooltip: Pick the closest match to what you sell. It sets default benchmarks and seasonality, for example higher Q4 costs for ecommerce.

regions.label: Region(s)
regions.tooltip: The countries you target. Ad costs vary a lot by country, so we plan each country separately when you have data for more than one.

month.label: Planning month
month.tooltip: The month you are planning for. Busy months like November and December usually cost more per impression.

currency.label: Currency
currency.tooltip: All money fields use this currency. We suggest one from your first region, and you can change it.

targetResults.tooltip: How many new clients (lead generation) or orders (ecommerce) you want each month. We work backwards from this to the budget.

monthlyBudget.label: Monthly budget available
monthlyBudget.tooltip: The most you can spend on ads in a month. We show what it can deliver and whether it is enough to exit the learning phase.

clientValue.label: Average client value
clientValue.tooltip: What a new client pays you on average: the package price or the first purchase. Find it in your CRM or sales records.

margin.label: Margin
margin.tooltip: Profit left after delivering the service, before ad costs. A 60% margin on 600 leaves 360 to spend on winning that client.

bookingRate.label: Booking rate
bookingRate.tooltip: Share of leads who book a call or consultation. Bookings ÷ leads, from your CRM or calendar.

showRate.label: Show-up rate
showRate.tooltip: Share of bookings who actually attend. Shows ÷ bookings.

closeRate.label: Close rate
closeRate.tooltip: Share of attendees who buy. Clients ÷ shows. With previous data we use your real funnel instead.

rateSource.label: Source of these rates
rateSource.tooltip: Where the booking, show-up and close rates come from. CRM data is the most reliable and gives a narrower range.

leadSource.label: Lead source
leadSource.tooltip: Instant forms collect leads inside Meta and are usually cheaper, but those leads book less often than landing page leads.

aov.label: Average order value (AOV)
aov.tooltip: Average revenue per order. For a new store, use your main product or bundle price.

productCost.label: Product cost per order
productCost.tooltip: What the products in an average order cost you, including packaging.

shipping.label: Shipping cost per order
shipping.tooltip: What you pay to ship an average order. Use 0 if the customer pays shipping in full.

paymentFee.label: Payment fees
paymentFee.tooltip: Payment processor fees as a share of the order value, often 2% to 4%.

returnRate.label: Return rate
returnRate.tooltip: Share of revenue lost to returns and refunds. Important for fashion, where it can be 20% or more.

ordersPerCustomer.label: Orders per customer
ordersPerCustomer.tooltip: Average number of orders a customer places over their lifetime. Used only if you judge profit on lifetime value.

judgeOn.label: Judge profit on
judgeOn.tooltip: First order is the safe default. Lifetime value lets you pay more per customer, but only if repeat orders are proven.

days.label: Date range (days)
days.tooltip: How many days the account data below covers. 30 days is a good default. Use the same range in Meta and Google.

retargetingAudience.label: Retargeting audience size
retargetingAudience.tooltip: Website visitors plus social engagers from the last 30 days. Find it in Meta Events Manager or your custom audiences.

gCost.label: Cost
gCost.tooltip: Google Ads → Campaigns → Cost for the same date range.

gConversions.label: Conversions
gConversions.tooltip: Google Ads → Campaigns → Conversions. Count only the primary conversion (lead or purchase).

gConversionValue.label: Conversion value
gConversionValue.tooltip: Google Ads → Campaigns → Conv. value. Revenue reported by Google for purchases.

gImpressionShare.label: Search impression share
gImpressionShare.tooltip: Google Ads → Columns → Competitive metrics → Search impr. share. The share of eligible searches where your ads showed.

gLostBudget.label: Search lost IS (budget)
gLostBudget.tooltip: Share of searches you missed because the budget ran out. This sets how much more Google can absorb.

gLostRank.label: Search lost IS (rank)
gLostRank.tooltip: Share of searches you missed because of low ad rank. More budget does not fix this, better bids and quality do.

gBrand.label: Do people search for your brand?
gBrand.tooltip: If people already search your brand name, we set aside a small brand campaign budget to protect those clicks.

eCpm.label: CPM
eCpm.tooltip: CPM is the cost per 1,000 impressions. Use Meta's estimate in Ads Manager, your other accounts or a published benchmark for your country.

eCtr.label: CTR (link)
eCtr.tooltip: Link click-through rate: link clicks ÷ impressions. 0.8% to 1.5% is common on Meta.

eCvr.tooltip: Share of link clicks that become a lead (landing page) or a purchase (store). Your website analytics is the best source.

eFormRate.label: Instant form completion rate
eFormRate.tooltip: Share of people who open the instant form and submit it. Often 10% to 20%.

eAtcRate.label: Add to cart → purchase rate
eAtcRate.tooltip: Share of add to carts that turn into purchases. Used to guide an Add to Cart test when the budget is small.

eDailyMin.label: Estimated daily results (min)
eDailyMin.tooltip: From the Meta ad set panel: the lower end of 'Estimated daily results'. Used only as a cross-check.

eDailyMax.label: Estimated daily results (max)
eDailyMax.tooltip: The upper end of Meta's 'Estimated daily results' for the same daily budget.

eDailyBudget.label: Daily budget used for that estimate
eDailyBudget.tooltip: The daily budget you entered in Meta when it showed the estimate above.

gKeywords.label: Main keywords
gKeywords.tooltip: Optional. The main search terms you plan to bid on, for your own reference.

gSearches.label: Monthly search volume
gSearches.tooltip: Total monthly searches for your keywords in your regions. Google Ads → Tools → Keyword Planner.

gBidLow.label: Top of page bid (low)
gBidLow.tooltip: Keyword Planner → 'Top of page bid (low range)'. We average the low and high bids as the expected cost per click.

gBidHigh.label: Top of page bid (high)
gBidHigh.tooltip: Keyword Planner → 'Top of page bid (high range)'.

gIS.label: Expected impression share
gIS.tooltip: Share of those searches where you expect to show. New accounts often reach 30% to 60%.

gCtrNew.label: Expected CTR
gCtrNew.tooltip: Clicks ÷ impressions on search ads. 3% to 7% is common for well-matched keywords.

gCvrNew.label: Expected conversion rate
gCvrNew.tooltip: Share of search clicks that convert. Search traffic usually converts better than social.

gBrandNew.label: Do people search for your brand?
gBrandNew.tooltip: If yes, we keep a small brand campaign so competitors do not take those clicks.

adSets.label: Planned number of Meta ad sets
adSets.tooltip: Each ad set needs about 50 results a week to exit learning. Fewer ad sets means more data per ad set.

creatives.label: Number of creatives to test
creatives.tooltip: Each creative needs some spend to prove itself, about 2.5 × your target cost per result.

testDays.label: Test duration (days)
testDays.tooltip: How long the first test runs before you decide to scale, optimize or stop. 14 days is a good default.

includeRetargeting.label: Include retargeting
includeRetargeting.tooltip: Show ads again to people who visited or engaged. For new accounts we add it after 2 to 4 weeks.

campaignName.label: Campaign name
campaignName.tooltip: Optional, to help you recognise the row.

budgetType.label: Budget type
budgetType.tooltip: CBO: Meta spreads one budget across ad sets. ABO: each ad set has its own budget. Advantage+: one automated campaign.

campaignAdSets.label: Number of ad sets
campaignAdSets.tooltip: Active ad sets in this campaign.

adSetsWithSpend.label: Ad sets getting meaningful spend
adSetsWithSpend.tooltip: In CBO, Meta often spends on only a few ad sets. Count the ones that get a real share of the budget.

rowCountry.label: Country
rowCountry.tooltip: The country this row covers. Leave empty if you have one row for all countries.

spend.label: Amount spent
spend.tooltip: Ads Manager → Columns → Performance → Amount spent.

reach.label: Reach
reach.tooltip: Ads Manager → Columns → Performance → Reach. Unique people who saw your ads.

linkClicks.label: Link clicks
linkClicks.tooltip: Ads Manager → Columns → Performance and clicks → Link clicks.

landingPageViews.label: Landing page views
landingPageViews.tooltip: Ads Manager → Columns → Performance and clicks → Landing page views. Needs the Meta pixel.

formLeads.label: Instant form leads
formLeads.tooltip: Ads Manager → Results for lead form campaigns (On-Facebook leads).

landingLeads.label: Landing page leads
landingLeads.tooltip: Website leads tracked by the pixel or your CRM.

bookings.label: Bookings (CRM)
bookings.tooltip: Calls or consultations booked from these leads, from your CRM or calendar.

addToCarts.label: Adds to cart
addToCarts.tooltip: Ads Manager → Columns → Conversions → Adds to cart.

checkouts.label: Checkouts initiated
checkouts.tooltip: Ads Manager → Columns → Conversions → Checkouts initiated.

purchases.label: Purchases
purchases.tooltip: Ads Manager → Columns → Conversions → Purchases. Your store is the source of truth if numbers differ.

learningThreshold.label: Meta learning threshold (results per ad set per week)
learningThreshold.tooltip: Meta needs about 50 optimisation events per ad set per week to exit the learning phase.

googleMinConversions.label: Google smart bidding minimum (conversions per campaign per 30 days)
googleMinConversions.tooltip: A common rule of thumb for smart bidding. Check Google's current guidance, as it changes.

minResultsForConfidence.label: Minimum results for confident data
minResultsForConfidence.tooltip: Below this many results we blend your cost with a benchmark and flag low confidence.

scalingPenalty.label: Cost increase per doubling of spend
scalingPenalty.tooltip: How much cost per result rises each time spend doubles. 15% is a common planning assumption.

profitBuffer.label: Profit buffer
profitBuffer.tooltip: Safety margin below break-even. The target cost is the maximum cost ÷ (1 + buffer).

newAccountPenalty.label: New account penalty
newAccountPenalty.tooltip: New accounts usually pay more at first. We add this to estimated costs.

creativeTestMultiplier.label: Creative testing spend per creative (× target cost)
creativeTestMultiplier.tooltip: Spend each creative gets to prove itself, as a multiple of your target cost per result.

scaleThreshold.label: Scale threshold (share of break-even)
scaleThreshold.tooltip: If the real cost after the test is at or below this share of your maximum, scale.

stopLossLow.label: Stop-loss low (× break-even)
stopLossLow.tooltip: Stop a campaign or creative that spends this multiple of your maximum cost with no results.

stopLossHigh.label: Stop-loss high (× break-even)
stopLossHigh.tooltip: Upper end of the stop-loss range.

retargetingViewsPerMonth.label: Retargeting views per person per month
retargetingViewsPerMonth.tooltip: How often each person in the retargeting audience should see your ads.

retargetingCap.label: Retargeting cap (share of Meta budget)
retargetingCap.tooltip: Retargeting never takes more than this share of the Meta budget.

minRetargetingAudience.label: Minimum retargeting audience
minRetargetingAudience.tooltip: Below this size, retargeting is skipped because it cannot deliver efficiently.

brandShare.label: Brand campaign share of Google budget
brandShare.tooltip: Share of the Google budget kept for a brand campaign when people search your brand.

maxStepIncrease.label: Max budget increase per step
maxStepIncrease.tooltip: Raise budgets by no more than this each step to avoid resetting learning.

stepDays.label: Days between budget steps
stepDays.tooltip: Wait this many days between budget increases.

rangeLow.label: {source}: low multiplier
rangeLow.tooltip: The optimistic end of the cost range for estimates from this source.

rangeHigh.label: {source}: high multiplier
rangeHigh.tooltip: The cautious end of the cost range for estimates from this source. Less reliable sources get a wider range.

errors.rowsRequired: Add at least one row of account data.
errors.reachGtImpressions: Reach cannot be higher than impressions.
errors.clicksGtImpressions: Clicks cannot be higher than impressions.
errors.lpvGtClicks: Landing page views cannot be higher than link clicks.
errors.bookingsGtLeads: Bookings cannot be higher than leads.
errors.showsGtBookings: Shows cannot be higher than bookings.
errors.clientsGtShows: Clients cannot be higher than shows.
errors.costsGteAov: Product cost, shipping, fees and returns add up to the order value or more, so there is no profit to spend on ads.
errors.adSetsSpendGtAdSets: Ad sets getting spend cannot be more than the number of ad sets.
errors.bidLowGtHigh: The low bid cannot be higher than the high bid.
errors.stopLossOrder: The low stop-loss cannot be higher than the high one.
errors.nicheFirst: Choose a niche in Setup first.

warnings.purchasesGtCheckouts: Purchases are higher than checkouts. Check your tracking.
warnings.ctrHigh: CTR above 10% is unusual. Check that you used link clicks.
warnings.cvrHigh: A conversion rate above 50% is unusual. Check the numbers.
warnings.frequencyHigh: Frequency is above 5. The audience may be tired of your ads.
warnings.fewResults: Only {results} results in this period (under {min}). We will blend with benchmarks and flag low confidence.

actions.exampleLoaded: Example data loaded for this mode.
actions.noScenarios: No saved scenarios yet. Save one to compare it later.
actions.compareHint: Tick up to {max} scenarios to compare them side by side.
actions.shareCopied: Share link copied. It contains only your planner inputs.
actions.shareFailed: Could not copy the link. Copy it from the address bar instead.

csv.title: Import a CSV export
csv.intro: Upload a Meta Ads Manager or Google Ads export. We match the columns, you confirm, then we fill the fields.
csv.imported: {rows, plural, one {Imported # row.} other {Imported # rows.}} Check the fields below.
csv.error: We could not read that file. Export it as CSV and try again.

benchmarks.title: My benchmarks
benchmarks.intro: Save numbers from your own accounts and reuse them for new clients in the same niche and region.
benchmarks.used: {count, plural, one {Filled from # of your saved rows.} other {Filled from # of your saved rows.}}
benchmarks.usedDefaults: No saved rows match yet, so we used placeholder benchmarks. Replace them with your own numbers.
benchmarks.none: No benchmarks available for this niche yet.
benchmarks.context: Saved with your current niche, region ({region}) and month ({month}).

crossCheck.implied: Meta's estimate implies a cost per result between {low} and {high}. Compare it with your estimates above.

seasonal.intro: Multipliers for {profile}. 1.0 means a normal month. These are editable estimates, not measured data.

advanced.benchmarksNote: Default benchmarks per niche and platform are placeholder values and should be replaced with real data.

compare.incomplete: This scenario has missing or invalid inputs.
